name: Indigenous knowledge
dimension: the aspect of a knowledge system the claim is about

objects.label: Ordering principles
objects.text: IK.O.A1 Ordering principles

objects.label: Whakapapa as ordering
objects.text: IK.O.A1.1 Whakapapa as ordering — genealogy as the principle that relates people, atua and the natural world. Whakapapa as human descent is HI; whakapapa of atua is RE.

objects.label: Categories of status
objects.text: IK.O.A1.2 Categories of status — tapu and noa as ordering categories outside rite (in rite, RE.O.A1.2).

objects.label: Cyclical and ancestral time
objects.text: IK.O.A1.3 Cyclical and ancestral time — "ka mua, ka muri" (walking backwards into the future) as a stated orientation (·S W8; ·M W13).

objects.label: Relations to land and waters
objects.text: IK.O.A2 Relations to land and waters

objects.label: Kaitiakitanga
objects.text: IK.O.A2.1 Kaitiakitanga — guardianship as obligation. Its measured environmental effect is EV.O.A4.4.

objects.label: Maramataka
objects.text: IK.O.A2.2 Maramataka — the lunar calendar as a system for timing activity. An ecological observation it records (a fish run) is BI or EA under W4; the system itself is IK.

objects.label: Place knowledge
objects.text: IK.O.A2.3 Place knowledge — names, boundaries and histories of places, held by mana whenua. The landform is EA; the dated event is HI.

objects.label: Governance and custom
objects.text: IK.O.A3 Governance and custom

objects.label: Tikanga as custom
objects.text: IK.O.A3.1 Tikanga as custom — correct practice in social life. In rite before atua it is RE.O.A3.1. As recognised by a state court it is LA.O.A1.3.

objects.label: Rangatiratanga
objects.text: IK.O.A3.2 Rangatiratanga — authority and self-determination as held. Its Treaty and legal dimension is LA.O.A4.4; its political dimension is PO.

objects.label: Marae kawa
objects.text: IK.O.A3.3 Marae kawa — the protocols of a particular marae (local, ·M).

objects.label: Customary institutions
objects.text: IK.O.A3.4 Customary institutions — rūnanga, hui as decision forums.

objects.label: Transmission
objects.text: IK.O.A4 Transmission

objects.label: Institutions of learning
objects.text: IK.O.A4.1 Institutions of learning — whare wānanga, past and present. Modern wānanga as tertiary institutions are ED.

objects.label: Oral and performed transmission
objects.text: IK.O.A4.2 Oral and performed transmission — kōrero tuku iho, mōteatea, haka. Their poetics are AR; their language is LN.

objects.label: Restricted knowledge
objects.text: IK.O.A4.3 Restricted knowledge — knowledge held by designated people and not for open classification. The pyramid records that restriction exists, never the content.

objects.label: Research and data
objects.text: IK.O.A5 Research and data

objects.label: Kaupapa Māori research
objects.text: IK.O.A5.1 Kaupapa Māori research — research by, with and for Māori, under Māori control (Smith, *Decolonizing Methodologies*, 1999).

objects.label: Data sovereignty
objects.text: IK.O.A5.2 Data sovereignty — Te Mana Raraunga principles; the CARE principles. The records framework is IS.O.A5.4.

objects.label: Consent and benefit
objects.text: IK.O.A5.3 Consent and benefit — Wai 262 (*Ko Aotearoa Tēnei*, 2011) on flora, fauna and mātauranga (UNVERIFIED date). Legal effect is LA.

methods.label: Hold and recite
methods.example: recitation of whakapapa by designated holders

warrants.defeaters: ·S: traced to recorded kōrero; ·M: held by the designated people

bridges_table: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander studies

sections.governing_thought:
Indigenous knowledge is exhausted by four faces of one pyramid: objects, methods, warrants and bridges.
Its objects divide into five aspects of a knowledge system: ordering principles, relations to land and waters, governance and custom, transmission, and research and data.
sections.key_line:
Dimension: **the aspect of a knowledge system the claim is about.** Order: from the system's principles to its relation with outside research.
1. Ordering principles
2. Relations to land and waters
3. Governance and custom
4. Transmission
5. Research and data

A people (iwi, hapū, nation) is a substrate, not a cell. A ·M sentence names its iwi or hapū, because authority is local.
sections.assignment_rules:
1. Place by the aspect of the knowledge system, then by mode (·S or ·M).
2. A measurement, a dated fact, a legal duty and a word's meaning keep their owners (BI, EA, HI, LA, LN). The tradition may be the record they cite.
3. A claim about rite before atua is RE; a claim about custom in social life is IK.
4. Tikanga recognised by a state court is LA.
5. Rongoā efficacy for a named condition is MD under W3; the rite of rongoā is RE or IK.
6. No residual "Indigenous" cell exists. A claim that fits no IK cell goes to its subject's owner.
7. Māori-led review may withhold any claim.

sections.crosswalk:
**ANZSRC 45** Indigenous studies has 20 groups (checked in p2_ANZSRC45.md): 4501–4506 Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander; 4507–4512 Māori; 4513–4518 Pacific Peoples; 4519 Indigenous data, methodologies and global studies; 4599 a residual.
Each people group pairs a people (substrate) with a topic. The topics land as follows: culture, language and history → IK.A1–A4, with HI and LN; education → ED; environmental knowledge → IK.A2; health and wellbeing → MD; law and governance → IK.A3 and LA; sciences → IK.A2 with BI and EA; 4519 → IK.A5.
Coverage: 19 of 20 land (as substrate × cell); 4599 is refused as a residual.
sections.validation:
Sizes: key line 5. Face O 5 cells + 16 sub-cells = 21. M roles 5. Heuristics 3. W rows 5, each split ·S/·M. B bridges 6.
Key line, word for word: Ordering principles. Relations to land and waters. Governance and custom. Transmission. Research and data.
CONTESTED: the whole pyramid. One alternative holds that mātauranga is a whole system owning its phenomena (ecology and health stay with the tradition). It is flagged here and not adopted. A second alternative holds that IK should not exist as a pyramid at all, and claims should be split by subject as in p2_ANZSRC45.md. Reviewers decide.
